newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to construct new gas storage facilities.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to construct new gas storage facilities.

text.p: Bulgaria will build new underground gas storage facilities to secure regular supplies to its neighbours, officials said on Thursday.

Vladimir Filipov, executive director of Bulgaria's state-owned gas distributor Bulgargas said the company had already started work on expanding the Chiren gas storage facility in northern Bulgaria from its current one billion cubic metres to more than two billion.
Apart from the Chiren expansion, Bulgargas plans to build two more gas storage sites to help Turkey and Greece overcome sharp falls in Russian gas supplies in cold winters, he said.

"The capacity of these facilities will be smaller (than Chiren) and we are seeking funds for their construction. World Bank officials have assured us the bank would consider granting funds for the construction," Filipov said during a regional meeting in Sofia.

One of the planned new underground storage facilities will use abandoned salt caverns in the village of Mirovo near the Devnya industrial region in northeastern Bulgaria. Its provisional capacity will be 300-500 million cubic metres. Natural gas was found under the caverns.
The location of the third facility has not been chosen yet but several ideas have been discussed, officials said.
"Our plans are to complete Chiren's expansion and the construction of Mirovo storage facility by the end of the century," Bulgargas chief expert Radi Ivanov said.
For the last 10 years a gas pipeline has linked Bulgaria with Turkey, which mainly depends on Russia for natural gas supplies.

Ivanov said Turkey's state pipeline company Botas had shown interest in using the Chiren and Mirovo gas storage facilities. Botas representative Mehmet Topdas said Turkish gas consumption was expected to increase rapidly in the next few years.
"We have come to see the Chiren facility and get more information on Bulgaria's gas storage. We have not decided anything yet," Topdas said.
The European Union Phare programme has earmarked 200,000 Ecus this year for the expansion of the underground Chiren facility, which has been operating for 22 years, Ivanov said.
Bulgaria's 2,200-km pipeline network, which includs 625 km of transit pipelines, receiving and transmitting gas from outside the country, has also a link with Greece and Macedonia.
Last September Greece started receiving Russian gas via Bulgaria and its Public Gas Corporation SA (DEPA) said it would receive more than one billion cubic metres in 1997.
Bulgaria has completed a pipeline to Macedonia which is filled with gas and waiting for its neighbour to complete pipeline construction on its territory.
Ivanov said Macedonia will start receiving its first deliveries of natural gas by the end of the year or the beginning of 1998.
